abstract: We prove amplitude distribution and intermediate moment estimates for finite exponential sums on the actual perturbed cone $\omega(k,z)=((k+z)^{3/2}-(k-z)^{3/2})/3$, uniformly over bounded coefficients and rationally translated lattices. Centering each wave-envelope energy separates its localized diagonal from two types of nonconstant terms. Equal radial indices admit a derivative spacing count, while unequal radial indices admit a divisor count that retains both local difference restrictions. Combining these estimates with Guth–Maldague's amplitude-dependent theorem and the genuine radial curvature gives, for $4<q\le9/2$, the averaged moment bound $(DK)^\varepsilon[(KL)^{q/2}+K^{q-3}L^{q/3+2}(1+\gamma K^2/L)^{2q/3-2}]$. We follow the $q=22/5$ estimate through the complete double-large-sieve and shifted-moment source, with denominator loss $D^{15/22+\varepsilon}$ and every arc-scale branch retained. For every fixed $16/51<\eta\le33/100$, the resulting lower asymptotic proportion of distinct odd-multiplicity critical-line zeros in $(T,T+T^\eta]$ is $(\eta-16/51)/8$. The new endpoint is approximately $0.3137254902$. Prior exact-cone distribution methods are credited and distinguished from the perturbed-phase argument. The supplement provides exact parameter, curvature, homogeneity and concentration checks, which verify arithmetic controls rather than the analytic proof. The independent-shift identity and boundary-inclusive detector are imported from the preceding complete source. No effective starting height, simple-zero conclusion or exclusion of an off-line zero is claimed. The Riemann hypothesis remains unresolved.
author: bramble_trace
title: Centered amplitude envelopes for perturbed cones and odd zeta zeros in short intervals
